+"""Record preparation steps.
+
+``prepare_record`` validates a record and applies a display function to its
+value; ``prepare`` is the default step using click's short-help condensing.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import typing as t
+
+from click.utils import make_default_short_help
+
+SHORT_HELP_MAX_LENGTH = 20
+
+
+def _validate(record: t.Any) -> tuple[str, t.Any, bool]:
+    if not isinstance(record, dict):
+        raise ValueError("record must be a dict")
+
+    key = record.get("key")
+
+    if not isinstance(key, str) or not key.strip():
+        raise ValueError("record key must be a nonempty string")
+
+    if "value" not in record:
+        raise ValueError("record must have a value entry")
+
+    enabled = record.get("enabled", True)
+
+    if not isinstance(enabled, bool):
+        raise ValueError("record enabled must be a bool")
+
+    return key.strip(), record["value"], enabled
+
+
+def prepare_record(
+    record: t.Any, display: t.Callable[[t.Any], t.Any]
+) -> dict[str, t.Any]:
+    """Validate ``record`` and return a new prepared dict whose ``display``
+    entry is ``display(value)``. The input is never mutated.
+    """
+    key, value, enabled = _validate(record)
+    return {
+        "key": key,
+        "value": value,
+        "display": display(value),
+        "enabled": enabled,
+    }
+
+
+def condense_help(value: str) -> str:
+    """Condense help text with click's default short-help semantics."""
+    return make_default_short_help(value, SHORT_HELP_MAX_LENGTH)
+
+
+def prepare(record: t.Any) -> dict[str, t.Any]:
+    return prepare_record(record, condense_help)

@@ -50,8 +50,31 @@ def prepare_record(
 
 def condense_help(value: str) -> str:
     """Condense help text with click's default short-help semantics."""
+    if not isinstance(value, str):
+        raise ValueError("record value must be a string")
+
     return make_default_short_help(value, SHORT_HELP_MAX_LENGTH)
 
 
 def prepare(record: t.Any) -> dict[str, t.Any]:
     return prepare_record(record, condense_help)
+
+
+def batch(records: t.Any) -> list[dict[str, t.Any]]:
+    """Prepare each record in order; duplicate trimmed keys raise ValueError."""
+    if not isinstance(records, list):
+        raise ValueError("records must be a list")
+
+    prepared = []
+    seen: set[str] = set()
+
+    for record in records:
+        item = prepare(record)
+
+        if item["key"] in seen:
+            raise ValueError(f"duplicate record key: {item['key']!r}")
+
+        seen.add(item["key"])
+        prepared.append(item)
+
+    return prepared
